run.question: Application-gateway server is returning 502 errors in the app-101 namespace. Please investigate.

report.summary: Investigated the reported 502s from an application gateway. Two blockers prevented any conclusion about the 502s. (1) No namespace named app-101 exists in the cluster: the namespaces are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, and a pod listing scoped to app-101 returned no objects (total_items_processed 0). The only application namespace is otel-demo, whose gateway-equivalent workload is the Envoy-based Deployment frontend-proxy (Service frontend-proxy, NodePort 8080); no object named application-gateway was found in any of the checks run. (2) The Prometheus and Jaeger data sources were unreachable for the whole run (every metrics/traces call between 16:29:21Z and 16:30:04Z returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no 502 status counts, request-rate, latency or trace evidence could be read at all. What Kubernetes state could be observed in otel-demo looked healthy at query time: 21 deployments each reporting 1 ready/available replica, 32 pods all Running with restartCount 0, all 26 Services having populated Endpoints (including frontend-proxy -> 10.244.0.22:8080 and frontend -> 10.244.0.20:8080), no NetworkPolicies, no Ingresses, and every fault-injection flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap still at defaultVariant off. Pod logs gave almost no runtime signal: frontend-proxy logged only startup (14:37:33Z) plus a 'shutting down parent after drain' line at 14:52:33Z that cannot be reconciled with its still-running, ready container (restartCount 0, no lastState), and frontend logged only Next.js startup ('Ready in 413ms') with no error lines. I fetched runbook application-gateway-troubleshooting and carried out what the tools allowed: Step 1 pod status (no application-gateway or app-101 objects; checked the otel-demo gateway frontend-proxy instead - Running/Ready), Step 2 error logs (frontend-proxy and frontend logs contained no error lines, but only 123 and 10 lines existed, so this is weak), Step 3 upstream service pods (frontend pod Running/Ready), Step 5 service endpoints (all 26 populated). Step 4 ('appg -t' config validation inside the pod) could not be carried out because no exec tool is available, and the 502 signal itself could not be checked because the metrics and trace sources were down. Conclusion is inconclusive, with no root cause assigned.

claims.text: No namespace named app-101 exists in the cluster; the namespaces returned are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo.
A pod listing scoped to namespace app-101 returned no objects (result_count 0, total_items_processed 0), consistent with that namespace not existing.

In namespace otel-demo the gateway-equivalent workload is Deployment frontend-proxy (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-frontend-proxy) exposed by Service frontend-proxy of type NodePort on port 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend-proxy; no service named application-gateway appears in the 26 Services returned.
All 21 Deployments in otel-demo reported readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1, and all 32 pods cluster-wide reported phase Running with container restartCount 0 at query time.
All 26 Services in otel-demo had populated Endpoints, including frontend-proxy at 10.244.0.22:8080 and its upstream frontend at 10.244.0.20:8080; no Service had an empty address set.

Pod frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n (ns otel-demo) is phase Running, all conditions True including Ready and ContainersReady, its frontend-proxy container ready=true started=true with restartCount 0, running since 2026-11-23T14:37:33Z and an empty lastState.

The frontend-proxy container log for the read 2026-10-24T16:29:14Z..2026-11-23T16:29:14Z contains 123 lines spanning 14:37:33.442Z to 14:52:33.474Z: Envoy startup (9 clusters, 1 listener, admin 0.0.0.0:10000, 'starting main dispatch loop', 'all dependencies initialized. starting workers') followed by one line '[2026-11-23 14:52:33.473][15][info][main] ... drain_manager_impl.cc:208] shutting down parent after drain'; no 5xx or upstream-error lines appear in those lines.
The frontend container log for the same window holds only 10 startup lines (14:37:27.103Z to 14:37:28.701Z), ending with 'Ready in 413ms'; no error lines were returned.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (key demo.flagd.json) holds 11 fault-injection flags - productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad - and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off'.
No Ingress objects and no NetworkPolicy objects exist anywhere in the cluster at query time (both listings returned 0 items).

All ReplicaSets in otel-demo were created between 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z and 14:38:03Z and each maintains ready=replicas=1; the only zero-replica ReplicaSets are the superseded otel-collector-845f9747bd and prometheus-547d4cbb8, and frontend-proxy's only ReplicaSet is frontend-proxy-844799bcdb, i.e. no later rollout of the gateway workload is visible.

Against a pod-crash or upstream-absence cause for 502s: every pod was Running with restartCount 0, every deployment had 1 ready/available replica, and every service (including frontend-proxy's upstream frontend) had a populated Endpoint address at query time.

Against a flag-driven fault-injection cause: all 11 flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap were at defaultVariant 'off' at query time, and no other object was observed applying a fault or change to the gateway workload.

Possibility that the gateway pod was evicted, OOMKilled or in CrashLoopBackOff was considered and not supported: frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n shows restartCount 0, empty lastState, phase Running and Ready=True, and no events were returned at all for the window.

If the reported 502s are real in this cluster, the failing hop would be frontend-proxy's upstream (Service frontend -> frontend-6c9bc688bf-ll8s7), since frontend-proxy is the only gateway in the environment and it is Running/Ready with a populated frontend endpoint; this is unverified because no trace, status-code or latency signal could be read from Jaeger or Prometheus.

The single Envoy 'shutting down parent after drain' line logged at 14:52:33Z suggests a graceful-shutdown sequence in the gateway process during the window, but it conflicts with the container's still-running state (ready, restartCount 0) and with the absence of a replacement pod, so a link to 502 responses cannot be established.

Restore or re-point the Prometheus and Jaeger data sources (both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call this Run), then check frontend-proxy and frontend 502 counts and upstream duration there - for example http_server_request_duration_seconds_count or traces_span_metrics_calls_total grouped by service_name and status_code - before drawing any conclusion.

Confirm the environment/namespace the 502 report came from: there is no app-101 namespace here, so verify whether the report refers to otel-demo (Envoy Deployment frontend-proxy) or to a different cluster, and re-run the investigation against that target.

gaps: The subject names namespace app-101, which does not exist in this cluster; nothing was found under that exact name, and the only application namespace present is otel-demo, investigated as a different entity.

The 502 responses themselves were never observed: the Prometheus source returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target between 16:29:21Z and 16:30:04Z), so http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket could not be read for any service or status code.

The Jaeger source also returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call (traces_search, traces_list_services, traces_list_operations between 16:29:21Z and 16:30:04Z), so no span, error tag or latency evidence for frontend-proxy or frontend exists in this Run.

The events listing across all namespaces returned no items (status no_data, total_items_processed 0), so crash, eviction, probe-miss or scale activity earlier in the window is unknown rather than absent.

A log query on frontend with an error/warning filter returned no lines (status no_data, 10 lines read and all filtered out), and a load-generator log query for 15:00Z-16:29Z returned no lines (status no_data); absence of matching lines there is not proof that nothing failed.

Only 123 log lines exist for frontend-proxy (startup plus one drain line, view marked incomplete with 23 lines omitted by the limit) and 10 lines for frontend (startup only); Envoy access logging and request-level error output were not available, so per-request 502 causes are unknown.

Runbook step 4 (validation of the gateway configuration with 'appg -t' inside the pod) could not be executed because no exec/attach tool is available in this Run, and no gateway configuration object exists as a ConfigMap in otel-demo to inspect instead.
The change_history integration is not integrated/available, so who or what changed cluster or workload state before 14:37Z could not be checked.
The frontend-proxy drain-shutdown log line at 14:52:33Z is unexplained: it is inconsistent with the container remaining running with restartCount 0, and no event or replacement pod accounts for it.
A deployment listing filtered for names matching gateway or app-101 returned nothing (status no_data), which only reflects the filter used, not evidence that such an object never existed.
next_steps: Re-run the metrics and trace checks once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable, starting with per-status-code request counts for frontend-proxy and its upstream frontend.
Confirm with the reporter which cluster/namespace the 502 reports came from, since app-101 does not exist here.

If exec access is approved, validate the Envoy configuration inside frontend-proxy and compare it with the frontend Service and port used for the upstream cluster, as the runbook's steps 4 and 5 suggest.
Watch frontend-proxy and frontend error rates around any future restart or drain event to test whether the 14:52:33Z drain line coincided with 5xx responses.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
